headline: The chief executive of the quantum company Q-Factor argues that a quantum computer can fail to be useful if the machinery that controls and reads its qubits cannot grow with it.
score_reason: Pool score 3 lowered by 1 because it is a company chief's opinion piece that promotes his own design, with no new result.
importance_line: Researchers and investors weighing quantum hardware designs get one company leader's view of the main obstacle to very large machines, but it is an opinion that also promotes his own firm's design and reports no new test results.
summary: In an opinion piece for Calcalist's CTech, Guy Raz, chief executive of quantum company Q-Factor, argues that the next hardware race will turn on whether control, measurement and error correction can grow along with the number of qubits, the machine's basic units, and presents his company's neutral-atom design as built for that. He says large qubit arrays and the key operations have so far been shown only separately, and joining them in one much larger machine is still the challenge.
notes: Opinion piece by the CEO of Q-Factor; read from the article data embedded in the page.
